title: Agentry
tagline: A Ledger-secured, Graph-powered autonomous purchase agent on Hedera Network
description:
A Ledger-secured, Graph-powered autonomous purchase agent. It pays for goods and services over Hedera's x402 rails, gates every payment behind a physical Ledger Nano approval, and reasons over its own on-chain purchase history — indexed by a subgraph — to suggest restocks and compare prices across vendors.
The commerce-agent architecture draws on established patterns from prior Zepto402/Maid402-lineage builds, but Vault402 itself — the Ledger payment gate, the Hedera/Blocky402 settlement path, the purchase-log contract, and the subgraph — is built fresh for this event.
how_its_made:
Ledger's role is scoped entirely to protecting the key behind the Hedera payment. It is not involved in the Ethereum Sepolia write at all — that's a separate, ordinary-key transaction, since Ethereum Sepolia's only job here is being a chain The Graph can index.

Decides — the agent identifies a purchase to make (restock or new order).
Unlocks the key — the Hedera operator's ECDSA key is encrypted at rest via the Ledger Key Ring (ring encrypt). The agent never holds it in plaintext; right before settlement it calls ring decrypt, which requires the physical Nano to be connected and confirm before releasing the key into memory. Note this is a gate on the key, not a hardware-produced signature — Hedera isn't a wallet-cli-supported currency, so the actual ECDSA signing happens in software once the key is released, not inside the device's secure element.
Settles — the agent uses that briefly-decrypted key to build and submit the payment through the Blocky402 facilitator, settling on Hedera testnet in HBAR.
Logs — the agent calls PurchaseLog.recordPurchase(...) on Ethereum Sepolia, using a standard key from .env — no Ledger involvement on this leg.
Indexes — a subgraph deployed to Ethereum Sepolia picks up the PurchaseLog event live.
Reasons — the agent queries its own purchase history through the Subgraph MCP in natural language, computes consumption patterns, and surfaces restock suggestions and cross-vendor price comparisons.
